wa_babylon_boulder.blurb: Babylon Boulder is a big block among the Empire Boulders in the Columbia Gorge, reached by following the path beyond the Roman Boulder until a large prow comes into view. It holds about eleven problems, and the bulk of them are friendly: a handful of V0 and V1 lines, a couple of V2 to V4 problems, then a V5 and one very hard V9 at the top end. The lower, downhill side offers easy highball climbing, which makes the V0 and V1 problems a fun tall warm-up rather than a low-to-the-ground circuit. Expect short, sit-and-send style bouldering with a mellow feel, best suited to climbers happy on moderate grades who want a few lines of real height.

wa_campus_traverse.blurb: Campus Traverse is a bouldering zone in Tumwater Canyon near Leavenworth, a short walk from the Swiftwater picnic area boulders. About a dozen problems are spread across a wide span, from a V0 up to a V10, but the real draw is the middle and upper range: several lines sit between V4 and V7, with a few V8 to V10 testpieces above them. The problems are tall and powerful, and the rock is kind on the skin. The wall gives welcome shade on hot days, so it works as a place to retreat when the nearby boulders are baking. Not a beginner spot; plan on it if you are climbing V4 and up.

wa_crack_du_jour.blurb: Crack du Jour is a small crag in the Eight Mile area of Icicle Canyon near Leavenworth, split into a short lower tier and a taller upper tier. It holds around eleven one-pitch routes, a roughly even mix of trad and sport, with grades running from 5.7 through the 5.8 and 5.9 range to a few 5.10s and a single 5.11. Expect cracks, slab and bolted face climbing on clean moderate lines, with chain anchors for lowering. The crag tends to stay shaded into the late morning in summer and is sheltered from wind. The hike up is steep and takes 20 to 30 minutes, so it suits climbers who do not mind a workout before a quiet day out.

wa_dome_the.blurb: The Dome is the main bouldering zone among the Bridge of the Gods Boulders in the Columbia Gorge, about an hour east of Portland. It is a fairly recently developed area with room for more new problems. Eleven problems are climbed so far, and the difficulty runs steep: a cluster in the V3 to V6 range, then a few much harder lines reaching into the V8 to V11 territory. That makes it better for stronger boulderers than for first-timers. The walk in is on gravel and rough tracks, around two-thirds of a mile each way, with no bushwhacking. Bring a map or GPS, as the way is easy to lose.
